mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the rank information coefficient over triggered periods is not statistically significant at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand but a nascent recovery in residential investment, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as sector rotation boosts cyclicals.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the cumulative gain is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 5.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a period of strong productivity growth as measured by INDPRO.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average by more than 1.5% signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA by > -1.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a simultaneous surge in export demand.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and acceleration of inflation, which increases real discount rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: dual inflation and rate hike regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when the economy is simultaneously experiencing a large positive supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth above 0.4%) combined with a stable consumer price index (CPIAUCSL change within ±0.2%) signals improved purchasing power without inflationary pressure, which supports durable goods consumption and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days via retail and industrial sector outperformance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate when credit conditions tighten sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the labor force participation rate above 62.5% for four consecutive months signals broader labor market engagement, which increases aggregate demand and supports earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < (62.5% - participation rate delta) for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of significant automation-driven productivity gains.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS falling below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months) signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue expectations for consumer-facing sectors and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a simultaneous surge in business investment.
